title: My FAIR Bioconductor
text:
Welcome
In the era of accelerating, AI-assisted, data generation and analysis, the need for open science practices, cross-community standards, and collaboration has never been more critical.

title: My FAIR Bioconductor
text:
What this book is
This book was initiated during a BioFAIR Collaboration Fest held at The Open University on 15-17 September 2026.
This book is a collaborative effort to provide guidance on applying the FAIR principles to Bioconductor assets, ensuring that they are Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable, within and beyond the Bioconductor ecosystem.
It takes Bioconductor as a case study of community developing open source software, data, and training resources, and provides guidance for users and developers to search for, access, and reuse Bioconductor functionality in other software ecosystems, starting with Galaxy and nf-core as established communities consuming and integrating Bioconductor functionality alongside other bioinformatics software.

title: My FAIR Bioconductor
text:
What this book is not
This book does not replace existing documentation and guidance for:

Development, Maintenance, and Peer Review of Bioconductor packages
Tool development and integration into Galaxy
Creating nf-core modules

Relevant documentation and guidance for these topics is maintained by the respective communities, and this book signposts to these resources where appropriate.

Definitions

Working definitions of Bioconductor, Galaxy, nf-core, WorkflowHub, and other relevant terms in relation to each other, avoiding jargon and implied knowledge to make the book inclusive and accessible to a wide audience.

Guidance

Processes, resources, and checklists to produce FAIR Bioconductor tool wrappers
Preferred file types for disk-based storage of R object and interoperability with other programming languages and software ecosystems.

section: 2.3 Galaxy file types for Bioconductor objects
text:
2.3 Galaxy file types for Bioconductor objects
How are R objects stored on disk in Galaxy? What are the preferred file types for interoperability with other programming languages and software ecosystems?
For example, this GitHub issue has been discussing insecure aspects of RData files. While those are the default file type for R objects, they are not interoperable with other programming languages and software ecosystems. Instead, the loom file format has gained popularity as a preferred file type for disk-based storage of R objects, and is interoperable with other programming languages and software ecosystems
